key_insight: PINNs give the best point-wise accuracy for a fixed Couette-flow case, while DeepONets learn a reusable solution operator that generalizes across slip and wall-velocity conditions.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that learned surrogates can accelerate real-time prediction and parametric studies of fluid systems with dynamic wall slip.
method: PINN solved the governing equations for a specific parameter set using physics constraints.
DeepONet was trained on high-fidelity Crank–Nicolson data to map boundary conditions to full flow fields.
Both approaches were benchmarked against numerical solutions for accuracy and speed.
evidence_signal: The PINN reached a relative L2 error of 0.083%, while DeepONet achieved 0.36% mean error on unseen cases and 0.88% on out-of-distribution signals, with about 540× speedup over the numerical solver.
watch_item: The PINN is not easily reusable across new parameter settings because it requires instance-specific retraining.
paper_title: Solution of the Newtonian plane Couette flow with dynamic wall slip using machine-learning methods
